prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has wrist fracture. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1470; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim purposes. Can you confirm you're okay to proceed?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Sugar Land, in the left lane. Traffic was backed up a bit. Then I felt a hard jolt from behind, and my car lurched forward into the intersection.

Q: Did you see the vehicle that hit you before the impact?

A: No. I was looking at the light and my phone was in the cradle on the dash. I never saw it coming.

Q: Were you able to get out of your vehicle afterward?

A: Yes, but I was shaken up. My right hand hurt right away, and I was holding my wrist against my chest.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: Yes. An ambulance took me to the emergency room. They did X-rays and said my wrist was fractured. They put it in a splint and told me I'd need to see an orthopedic specialist.

Q: Do you know if the other driver was cited or said anything at the scene?

A: The officer took the other driver's information and wrote a report. I think the driver said they had looked down at their radio and didn't brake in time. I didn't hear that myself, though. That's just what the officer told me.

Q: Have you had any follow-up treatment since?

A: Yes, I've seen the specialist twice. They're talking about a cast for several weeks and possibly physical therapy after that. I'm not able to drive much right now, and I've missed a few days of work.

Q: Is there anything else you think I should know about the accident or your injuries?

A: Not that I can think of. My neck is a little sore too, but I'm not sure if that's connected. I'll keep you posted.

Q: Thank you. We'll follow up once we've reviewed the police report and your medical records. Have a good day.

A: Thanks. You too.
